studies.title: The Point: Advanced Air Mobility Vertiport Feasibility Study
studies.publisher: Point of the Mountain State Land Authority
studies.place: Draper (The Point, former state prison site)
studies.summary: Vertiport feasibility study for The Point, the 600-acre state-owned innovation community in Draper on the former prison site. It covers trip demand and usage projections, ride sharing in a vertiport network, drone operations and airspace, vertiport technical feasibility and AAM economic benefits.
studies.notes: Final study, November 2025, posted by UAM Geomatics (NEXA). The 2024 announcement is at utahbusiness.com.

studies.title: Virginia Air Transportation System Plan (VATSP) Update
studies.summary: AAM section (Part 1 Ch. 2 Goal 5 / Objective 5.1 (AAM performance measures); Ch. 4 'Issues Affecting Virginia Airports': 'Advanced Air Mobility (AAM)' pp. 4-5 to 4-8 and 'Vertiports' pp. 4-8 to 4-10; Ch. 6 Inventory p. 6-6 (AAM/eVTOL readiness survey); Ch. 7 p. 7-55 Table 7-25 (airports with eVTOL charging); Ch. 10 funding-eligibility mention). Named AAM and Vertiport sections describe UAM/RAM concepts, eVTOL integration, vertiport siting (on-airport vs purpose-built, airside vs landside) and FAA EB 105; Goal 5 sets measures for AAM population coverage and the share of airports planning eVTOL/electric operations, and the airport survey found 23% of system airports had begun provisions for eVTOL charging.

studies.title: Advanced Air Mobility Aircraft Plan
studies.authors_or_consultant: Mead & Hunt (consultant per 2024 RFQ award packet)
studies.summary: Plan required by ESHB 1125. It covers AAM feasibility, infrastructure, regulation and economic effects in Washington. It finds that GA airports and heliports can be adapted at first, but new vertiports will be needed (fewer than 30% of heliports meet EB 105).
studies.notes: Cover says April 2025; file posted June 2025 as 'May2025'. Developed with a Technical Advisory Committee. Consultant attribution from https://appstest.wsdot.wa.gov/publications/fulltext/design/ConsultantSrvs/2024-Air-Mobility-Aircraft-Plan-PacketA-Mead-Hunt.pdf (not opened).

studies.title: Vertiports Land Use Compatibility Supplement (to the Airports and Compatible Land Use Guidebook)
studies.summary: Land use guidance for vertiports. It sets three compatibility zones based on aircraft altitude, noise, downwash and risk, and gives land use tables for local planners.

studies.title: Washington Aviation System Plan (WASP)
studies.authors_or_consultant: Kimley-Horn (prime, Seattle), in cooperation with Cascadia Consulting Group, Connico, Hovecon, Marr Arnold Planning, and Ricondo & Associates (per the Executive Summary title page)
studies.summary: AAM chapter (Final Report (Dec 2025) has an Emerging Trends chapter (listed in the Executive Summary source note); Executive Summary Section 3 'Emerging Aviation and Transportation Trends' (p. 5), Section 4 Innovation goal (p. 6), Section 6 takeaways (p. 8)). The plan names electric and alternate-propulsion aircraft, UAS, eVTOL and STOL aircraft, low-altitude airspace management, microgrids and EV charging, and multimodal hubs as trends that could change airport needs. It calls cost the main barrier and calls for coordination with utilities and agencies on energy supply, charging and fueling, and airspace. The Innovation goal's policies prepare airports for AAM, UAS, STOL/eVTOL and hydrogen aircraft. Press coverage (State Aviation Journal, May 2026) says the update adds an analysis of AAM and infrastructure needs and covers Grant County International Airport as a testing and research hub.
